result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers put rent next to the price index and show the gap without stating the roughly 12% real increase. A gives concrete dollar framing ($1,564 if rent had kept pace, $180 more a month), but it relies on a detached legend, one end label is clipped, and its title shows only the nominal 48%. B's title states both numbers in plain words, labels each line directly at its end, and notes that its axis starts at 100, though it shows an index rather than dollars on the axis and one start label overlaps the line. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers compare rent to the regional price index, but neither states the roughly 12% real increase; both show 48% against about 33%, so the gap is visible. B works better for a flyer: it uses a dollar axis and says rent would be $180 a month lower if it had only kept pace with prices. A plots both lines as an index, so its axis has no dollar units, though its lines are labeled directly. B's weaknesses are a detached legend, a clipped 'tracking prices' label and a y-axis starting at $1,000; it states the $1,000 baseline but doesn't justify it.
